evals.prompt: I have a plain C# DamageCalculator class in my Unity project (Assets/_Project/Scripts/Gameplay/DamageCalculator.cs, inside the Gameplay asmdef) that computes damage from attack power, defense, and a critical multiplier. Write tests for it.
evals.expected_output: EditMode NUnit tests in a test assembly: an EditMode test asmdef (Editor-only, referencing the Gameplay assembly and nunit.framework.dll), [Test] methods using Arrange-Act-Assert with NUnit constraint syntax and descriptive names, plus instructions to run them headlessly in batchmode.
expectations: Chooses EditMode tests (not PlayMode) because DamageCalculator is pure C# logic with no Unity lifecycle
Creates or describes a test assembly definition (.asmdef) that references the production Gameplay assembly and nunit.framework.dll, with includePlatforms set to Editor
Tests follow Arrange-Act-Assert structure with descriptive names like Method_ExpectedBehavior_WhenCondition
Assertions use NUnit constraint syntax such as Assert.That(x, Is.EqualTo(y))
Explains how to run the tests from the command line with Unity -batchmode -runTests -testPlatform EditMode -testResults, or via scripts/run_unity_tests.py

evals.prompt: Add a test that verifies my player actually jumps: PlayerController is a MonoBehaviour with a Rigidbody, and calling Jump() should make it move upward over the next physics frames.
evals.expected_output: A PlayMode [UnityTest] coroutine test that creates the player, calls Jump(), yields physics frames (WaitForFixedUpdate / yield return null), asserts upward movement with NUnit constraints, and cleans up spawned objects.
expectations: Chooses a PlayMode test because the behavior depends on MonoBehaviour/Rigidbody physics across frames
Uses [UnityTest] with an IEnumerator return type and yields frames (e.g., WaitForFixedUpdate or yield return null) before asserting
Places the test in a PlayMode test assembly (.asmdef) separate from EditMode tests
Asserts the upward movement with NUnit constraint syntax (e.g., Is.GreaterThan on the y position or velocity)
Destroys spawned GameObjects at the end of the test so tests remain independent
Mentions running the suite via batchmode with -testPlatform PlayMode

evals.prompt: Set up an automated test run for my Unity project in CI so the build fails when any test fails. We cannot open the Unity editor on the CI machine.
evals.expected_output: A batchmode CLI test step: locating the Unity executable (matching ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt, default Hub paths per OS or UNITY_PATH/--unity-bin), invoking Unity with -batchmode -runTests -testPlatform -testResults -logFile -, parsing the NUnit XML, and failing the job on any failed test-case, iterating until green.
expectations: Uses Unity batchmode CLI: -batchmode -projectPath -runTests -testPlatform -testResults with -logFile - for streamed logs, and does not add -quit alongside -runTests

Explains locating the Unity executable: --unity-bin or UNITY_PATH first, then default Hub install paths (C:/Program Files/Unity/Hub/Editor/<version>/Editor/Unity.exe on Windows with forward slashes, /Applications/Unity/Hub/Editor/... on macOS), matching the version in ProjectSettings/ProjectVersion.txt
Runs or recommends running both EditMode and PlayMode platforms, or justifies the chosen platform
Parses the NUnit results XML (test-run attributes and failed test-case nodes) to decide pass/fail instead of relying only on the process exit code, e.g., via scripts/run_unity_tests.py
CI step exits non-zero when any test fails, and the workflow is: run, read failure messages, fix, re-run until green
Notes the failure mode when no results file is produced (compile errors or another editor instance holding the project lock)
